comparison: Both evaluate methodological approach and dataset quality (C4, C19-C21, C25, C115-C122). OpenEval focuses on technical details and quantitative outcomes. Peer review (R1) combines these claims with quality control procedures (C123-C129) and emphasizes the large dataset as a strength. Both find the methodology SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R19 evaluates quality control and normalization procedures (C123-C129) separately. Peer review R1 groups these with the broader methodological approach (C4, C19-C21, C25, C115-C122). Both find these procedures SUPPORTED and appropriate for snRNA-seq data.

Perfect alignment on continuum framework and territory/neighborhood classification (C5-C6, C40-C41). Both evaluations find the conceptual approach SUPPORTED by clustering analysis and UMAP visualizations. Reviewers accepted the continuum interpretation without challenge.

Both address Sox6 territory characterization (C42-C46, C51). OpenEval includes validation claims (C100-C101) while peer review focuses on core territory findings. Both find claims SUPPORTED and consistent with previous literature. Peer review notes consistency with prior work.

OpenEval R3 includes stereological validation (C100-C101) that peer review R10 also addresses. Both evaluations find the stoichiometry validation SUPPORTED and note consistency with independent counts.

Minimal overlap on anatomical localization (C47-C48). OpenEval R4 addresses broader anatomical characterization (C47-C57) while peer review R3 focuses on Sox6 territory. Both find their respective claims SUPPORTED by in situ and immunohistochemistry data.

Both address Gad2 territory characterization (C49-C50, C55). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by marker gene expression. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting need for better contextualization within spatial topology literature, though data itself not disputed.

OpenEval R4 includes anatomical localization claims (C52-C54, C56-C57) that peer review R5 addresses as novel territory identifications. Both find these SUPPORTED by in situ hybridization and anatomical mapping.

Both address novel territory findings (C102-C104). OpenEval emphasizes Pcsk6 territory and Ebf1 subdivision as novel. Peer review accepts these as novel contributions supported by gene expression and anatomical data. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Perfect alignment on lesion model and vulnerability findings (C22-C24, C58, C63-C69). Both find claims SUPPORTED by quantitative analysis and statistical testing. Peer review explicitly endorses vulnerability findings as major contribution, including VTA vulnerability.

Both address gene module identification (C70-C74, C77-C78). OpenEval emphasizes statistical validation and Slc6a3 exclusion. Peer review accepts gene modules as key contribution without challenging statistical approach. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R11 addresses mechanistic connections for vulnerability genes (C75-C76, C107-C111). Peer review R7 accepts gene module findings broadly. Minimal direct overlap on C75-C76 (Slc6a3 mechanism). Both find claims SUPPORTED though OpenEval notes some connections are speculative.

Both address candidate vulnerability and resilience genes (C107-C111 overlap with C106-C111). OpenEval notes some connections are speculative. Peer review accepts candidates as major contribution supported by literature. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on VGLUT2 connection (C106). OpenEval R17 addresses specific vulnerability patterns. Peer review R14 discusses VGLUT2-expressing resilient neighborhoods in context of spatial topology. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address ML-cluster characterization (C79-C87). OpenEval emphasizes clustering analysis, UMAP integration, and in situ validation. Peer review accepts ML-clusters without challenge, noting analysis satisfied reviewer concerns. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address stress response interpretation of ML-clusters (C88-C91). OpenEval connects gene expression to stress pathways via citations. Peer review accepts stress response interpretation as part of endorsed ML-cluster framework. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address control comparison showing surviving neurons not dramatically altered (C92-C93). OpenEval emphasizes UMAP visualization and differential expression. Peer review accepts control as adequate validation. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address consistent sampling and surviving neuron characterization (C61-C62). OpenEval R8 groups with control comparison. Peer review R11 emphasizes importance for establishing molecular identity maintenance. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address statistical validation of consistent sampling (C60). OpenEval emphasizes this addresses sampling bias concerns. Peer review implicitly accepts as part of surviving neuron characterization. Both find claim SUPPORTED.

Both address cross-species integration (C94-C99). OpenEval emphasizes UMAP visualization and quantitative mapping. Peer review accepts mouse-human integration and stoichiometry validation (C100-C101 also addressed). Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address clustering workflow and cell type identification (C26-C29, C33-C36). OpenEval includes lesion-specific cluster identification (C37-C39). Peer review accepts clustering approach without challenge. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address initial lesion-specific cluster identification (C37-C39). OpenEval notes these are later characterized as ML-clusters. Peer review accepts as part of clustering workflow. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Perfect alignment on inclusion criteria and rare discordant cells (C30-C32). Both find claims SUPPORTED by histological analysis and citation. Peer review notes importance for understanding dopamine neuron inclusion criteria.

Perfect alignment on experimental design rationale and model limitations (C112-C114). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes timing justification and appropriate interpretation. Peer review accepts rationale without challenge.

Perfect alignment on background knowledge about mDA neuron diversity and disease relevance (C1-C3, C9-C12). Both find claims SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. Peer review affirms relevance by calling study 'important' for understanding heterogeneity and vulnerability.

Perfect alignment on methodological context and snRNA-seq advantages (C13-C18). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly endorses snRNA-seq advantages, noting superiority for reducing sampling bias and enabling large cell numbers.

Perfect alignment on overall study design and objectives (C7-C8). Both find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes objectives fulfilled by results. Peer review affirms anatomical localization and lesion analysis approach not challenged.
